planting.note: Plant in rich, consistently moist garden soil in part sun to full sun with good air circulation to deter powdery mildew.

directions: Leading Lady Amethyst produces light amethyst-purple whorls of tubular flowers on a compact, mounding clump in early summer. The dwarf habit keeps the series tidy at the front of a border or in containers without the legginess of older bee balm varieties. Fragrant foliage accompanies the blooms, and the dense growth benefits from good air circulation to resist mildew. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds visit the nectar-rich flowers readily.

planting.note: Plant in rich, moist soil in part sun to full sun; good air circulation helps prevent powdery mildew on the dense foliage.

directions: This compact Leading Lady selection covers a dense, mounding clump in bright pink bee-balm flowers during early summer. At just 10-14 inches tall it stays front-of-border friendly while spreading wider than it grows, making a solid groundcover of fragrant foliage. The dwarf habit was bred for garden performance without sacrificing flower power. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds are frequent visitors, while deer tend to leave it alone.

planting.note: Plant in rich, moist soil in part sun to full sun; the compact Pardon Me series shows improved mildew resistance over older bee balm types.

directions: Pardon My Rose carries intense rose-pink flower heads above fragrant, aromatic foliage on a compact clump that stays well-behaved at the front of a border. It is part of the mildew-resistant Pardon Me breeding line, bred specifically for tidier habit and cleaner foliage than heirloom bee balms. Summer blooms draw bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds in steady numbers. Deer generally avoid the pungent leaves.

planting.note: Plant in rich, moist soil in part sun to full sun; well-branched stems and good air circulation support a strong rebloom flush.

directions: Upscale Lavender Taffeta bears dark lavender-purple blooms over shiny, dark green foliage on a medium-height, well-branched clump. The branching habit is bred to push out a reliable second flush of flowers rather than a single summer peak. Fragrant flowers and leaves draw bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds through the season. It is deer-resistant and performs best with good air circulation to limit mildew.

planting.note: Plant in rich, moist soil in part sun to full sun; good air circulation helps the well-branched stems resist mildew.

directions: Large, 3.5-inch fluorescent pink flowers with lighter pink interiors give Upscale Pink Chenille a vivid two-tone glow on a medium-height, clump-forming plant. Well-branched stems extend bloom into a second flush rather than fading after one flowering cycle. Fragrant flowers and aromatic foliage make it a magnet for bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Deer generally pass it by.

planting.note: Plant in rich, moist soil in part sun to full sun; this is the tallest Upscale selection, so allow room at the back of the border.

directions: The tallest member of the Upscale series, Red Velvet opens large cherry-red flowers above bronze-tinted new foliage on well-branched, clump-forming stems. A strong second flush of bloom follows the first flowering cycle, stretching color later into the season. Fragrant flowers and foliage draw bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds, while deer tend to avoid it. Give it room at the back of a border where its height can be an asset.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; drought tolerant once established, leave seed heads standing for winter bird interest.

directions: Frankly Scarlet opens bright scarlet-orange daisy flowers above dark green foliage on an upright clump, part of the Color Coded breeding line selected for saturated, true colors. Once established it tolerates drought and average soils with minimal fuss. Bees and butterflies work the blooms all summer, and left-standing seed heads feed birds through winter. Deer generally leave the coarse foliage alone.

common_name: Color Coded One in a Melon Coneflower

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; adapts to average, fertile, or poor soils and tolerates light shade.

directions: One in a Melon produces large, 5 to 5.5 inch melon-colored flowers with matching melon cones, the overlapping petals held nearly horizontal for a full, rounded look. The tall, upright clump adapts to a wide range of soils and tolerates some light shade while performing best in full sun. Fragrant blooms attract bees and butterflies through summer and fall, and standing seed heads feed birds into winter. Deer tend to avoid the bristly foliage.

common_name: Color Coded Orange You Awesome Coneflower

planting.note: Plant in average to fertile, well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; drought tolerant once established.

directions: Orange You Awesome bears large tangerine-orange flowers with dark, contrasting cones above dense dark green foliage on a compact, upright clump. Part of the Color Coded line bred for intensely saturated flower color, it blooms steadily from summer through fall. Bees and butterflies visit regularly, and mature seed heads left standing provide winter food for birds. The deer-resistant foliage and drought tolerance once established make it an easy-care border choice.

common_name: Color Coded The Fuchsia Is Bright Coneflower

planting.note: Plant in poor to fertile, well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; tolerates a wide pH range and becomes drought tolerant once established.

directions: The Fuchsia is Bright lives up to its playful name with 4.5-inch fuchsia-pink flowers held over a dark charcoal cone and stems, the overlapping petals set nearly horizontal for a bold, full-faced bloom. The compact upright clump tolerates poor, average, or fertile soil across a wide pH range. Fragrant flowers draw bees and butterflies from summer through fall, and the plant resists deer browsing. It works equally well massed in a border or cut for arrangements.

common_name: Color Coded Yellow My Darling Coneflower

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; tolerates acidic to alkaline pH and becomes drought tolerant once established.

directions: Yellow My Darling opens rich yellow flowers that soften to a creamy yellow as they age, giving a single clump a two-tone effect over its bloom cycle. The upright, medium-height habit suits borders and mixed perennial beds in well-drained soil. Fragrant flowers draw bees and butterflies, and seed heads left standing through winter feed birds. The plant is deer-resistant and tolerates a broad range of soil pH.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; drought tolerant once established.

directions: Butter Pecan produces fully double, 4-inch soft melon-yellow flowers with broad, horizontal ray petals that maximize apparent flower size, part of the Double Coded series bred for fully doubled blooms. The compact, upright clump stays fragrant and floriferous from summer through fall. As a native North American perennial it resists deer and supports a steady stream of pollinating insects. It performs best in well-drained soil and tolerates drought once established.

planting.note: A new 2026 Proven Winners introduction; plant in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun, drought tolerant once established.

directions: Coral Cranberry is a new 2026 Proven Winners selection carrying bright coral-pink, fully double flowers with broad, horizontal ray petals that fill out the bloom. Excellent branching keeps the compact clump smothered in flowers, ideal for the front of a border. Fragrant blooms attract pollinators through summer and fall, and the plant is deer-resistant and drought tolerant once established. It also holds up well as a cut or dried flower.

planting.note: Plant in sunny, well-drained soil; tolerates some partial shade, drought tolerant once established.

directions: Raspberry Beret is a fully double coneflower with intense raspberry-pink flowers, 4 inches wide, with matching ray petals throughout the bloom. Prolific flower production runs from summer through fall on an upright, well-branched clump suited to borders and containers. It tolerates hot, sunny sites and some partial shade, growing drought tolerant once established. Native to North America, it resists deer and keeps pollinators busy all season.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; compact size suits containers and small-space borders.

directions: Firefinch, from the Summersong breeding line, shows warm reddish-orange to pinkish-red daisy flowers on a neat, upright, compact clump. Its short stature makes it a good filler for containers and the front of smaller borders where taller coneflowers would overwhelm the space. Fragrant blooms run from summer through fall, drawing bees and butterflies while the coarse foliage discourages deer. It becomes notably drought tolerant once established.

planting.note: Plant in full sun in average, well-drained soil; heat and drought tolerant once established.

directions: PowWow White holds slightly creamy, buttery-white petals that drape downward from a prominent central cone, with blooms that resist browning and stay fresh for weeks. The compact, upright habit keeps the plant tidy in beds and containers without staking. It tolerates heat and drought once established, making it dependable in exposed sunny sites. Butterflies visit the blooms through the long summer-into-fall flowering season.

planting.note: Plant in average to dry, well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; tolerates hot, windy sites and drought once established.

directions: Delicious Candy produces fuchsia-pink, pom-pom-style double flowers with a ring of single ray petals beneath the dense cone, giving each bloom a layered look. The upright, medium-height clump tolerates hot, windy sites and average to dry soil once established. Butterflies are drawn to the fragrant blooms, while deer tend to avoid the plant. It works well as a border accent, container filler, or cut flower.

planting.note: Grow as a tender perennial in zones 9-11 or as a warm-season annual nectar plant elsewhere; plant in part sun to full sun with average water.

directions: Monarch's Banquet opens bright orange-red flower clusters on an upright tropical milkweed prized as a top-tier nectar source for monarch butterflies. Fragrant blooms also draw bees and hummingbirds through a long warm-season flowering window. Hardy as a perennial only in zones 9-11, it is widely grown elsewhere as a seasonal pollinator plant in beds and containers. It is easy to grow and resists deer browsing.

planting.note: Plant in dry to well-drained, neutral-pH soil in full sun; light winter mulch helps in colder parts of its range.

directions: Quartz Amethyst carries lavender-purple tubular flowers that rebloom through the season on an upright, well-sized clump. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil, tolerating both drought and salt once established. Bees and hummingbirds visit the flowers steadily from early summer onward. A light winter mulch helps it through cold snaps at the northern edge of its range.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; removing spent flower stems encourages continued bloom through the season.

directions: Cherry Sparks produces oversized cherry-red bells with contrasting white throats on an upright, native-origin penstemon. Because its flowers are sterile and set no seed, the plant channels its energy into a much longer bloom window than typical beardtongues, flowering from spring through summer. Hummingbirds, butterflies, and bees all work the tubular flowers readily. Deadheading spent stems keeps the display going through the heat of summer.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; drought tolerant once established and well suited to border fronts and containers.

directions: Rock Candy Light Pink stacks soft pink, bell-shaped flowers on tightly packed, compact flower spikes, part of a dwarf Penstemon barbatus series bred for small-space gardens. The low, uniform habit suits the front of a border, rock gardens, or mixed containers. It is heat and drought tolerant once established, needing little more than full sun and well-drained soil. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds all visit the tubular blooms.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; monthly fertilizing supports the large habit, and removing spent stems extends bloom.

directions: Summit Sweets Purple is a large, tall beardtongue carrying purple tubular flowers from spring through summer on an upright, back-of-border profile. It is both heat and drought tolerant, thriving in full sun with well-drained soil and benefiting from monthly fertilizing. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds visit the flower spikes steadily, and the blooms hold up well as cut flowers. Removing spent stems keeps the display coming.

planting.note: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; low water needs once established make it ideal for xeric borders.

directions: Arizona Sandstone forms a compact, mounding clump studded with vivid orange tubular flowers from spring through fall. Its low water needs and heat tolerance suit hot, sunny borders, rock gardens, and containers where many perennials struggle. Hummingbirds and butterflies visit the nectar-rich spikes throughout the long bloom season, while deer tend to avoid the aromatic foliage. It needs little more than full sun and sharp drainage to thrive.

planting.note: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; dislikes wet conditions and does not need deadheading to keep blooming.

directions: Maestro Gold sends up coral-pink flower spikes continuously from spring through fall without any deadheading required. The upright clump is drought tolerant and heat-loving but resents soggy soil, so sharp drainage is essential. Hummingbirds find the blooms especially irresistible, and bees and butterflies visit regularly too. Deer generally avoid the aromatic foliage.

planting.note: Grow as a perennial in zones 9-10 or as a warm-season annual filler elsewhere; plant in full sun with average water.

directions: Cherry Lemonade forms a low, mounded dome of red-toned daisy flowers over fine, ferny foliage, well suited to container edges or small-space landscape fillers. It is easy to grow, needing only full sun and average water to flower steadily. Hardy as a true perennial only in the warmest zones, it is grown as a seasonal bedding plant elsewhere. Pollinating insects visit the abundant small blooms through the growing season.

planting.note: Plant in full sun in average to poor, well-drained soil; drought tolerant once established and blooms early through late summer.

directions: Uptick Cream & Red opens cream-colored daisy flowers with contrasting dark red centers on a neat, mounded clump that blooms from early through late summer. It is adaptable to average, fertile, or poor soils and tolerates both acidic and neutral pH, growing drought tolerant once established. Bees and butterflies visit the bicolor blooms readily, while deer tend to leave it alone. It suits border edges, containers, and cut-flower use equally well.
